title: Add a card-finder skill and curated card list for golden tests
description:
The `golden-test` skill now pushes authors toward tighter, lower-noise scenarios, but it still assumes the author already knows which Magic cards best exercise a mechanic. In practice that means too much trial-and-error: finding the right fast mana, zero-mana permanents, clone targets, oddball timing cards, or compact combo pieces still depends on personal card knowledge instead of a repeatable workflow.

There is already usable Scryfall infrastructure in the repo (`scripts/scryfall.py`) plus existing skill/docs context for golden authoring, but nothing ties them together into a focused "find me the right cards for this test" workflow.

Follow-up scope:
- Create a dedicated skill for finding cards with particular properties for test construction, likely using Scryfall searches and/or small repo helpers around `scripts/scryfall.py`.
- Make that skill explicitly useful for golden-test authors: given a mechanic like "cheap clone target", "free mana", "forced trigger", or "single-card graveyard setup", it should help surface a short list of good candidates quickly.
- Add a convenient curated reference of high-value cards for golden tests in a repo-local place (doc, skill asset, or similar) so common patterns do not require a fresh search every time. That list should call out why each card is useful in tests, not just name cards.
- Update the `golden-test` skill to point at the new card-finding workflow/reference so the two skills work together instead of living separately.

The goal is to make good golden-test deck design reproducible. We should not rely on the model or the author happening to remember that `Black Lotus`, `Lotus Petal`, `Memnite`, `Dark Depths`, or some weird one-off enabler exists when a compact scenario depends on it.
